InvestNorthwise.text:
$NBIS gets a subtle capital allocation advantage from customer prepayments, but the advantage depends entirely on what Nebius gives customers in exchange for the cash.

The tension shows up in the contract mix, where Base weighted marginal pricing rises from $21.6M per MW in 2027 to $22.36M by 2030 as scarcity capacity expands, while the financing quality of that marginal MW deteriorates.

That dynamic makes our Bear case unusually interesting, because management responds to tighter financing by shifting toward long-duration investment-grade customers, accepting lower headline pricing in exchange for stronger prepayments and lender-quality collateral.

Customer prepayments can therefore be expensive financing, but the public disclosures cannot reveal their true economic cost because nobody knows the counterfactual price for identical capacity without prepayment, so our framework brackets the concession instead.

At a $22.5M reference contract, $50M of capex, 60% prepayment coverage, and a three-year term, the key thresholds are roughly 4.47% versus secured debt and 12% versus an 18% equity hurdle, turning prepayment economics into a decision rule rather than a guessed interest rate.

InvestNorthwise.text:
The capacity-versus-revenue argument with Jim Chanos around $NBIS needs one boring thing before it needs a verdict: matching dates.

Here's an illustrative cluster. Ten megawatts begin billing on November 1 at an annual pace of $12M per MW. Two months produce $20M of revenue. Divide that year's $20M by the 10 MW standing there in December and you get $2M per MW.

Nothing in the example requires weak pricing. The cluster is earning at the assumed $12M annual pace; it simply wasn't billing for twelve months. Conversely, annualising the two strong months and calling the result revenue already earned would overstate the income statement.

SpaceX adds further distinctions. A power agreement can refer to a future project. Installed hardware may still need commissioning and customer acceptance. Some accepted compute serves internal products instead of an outside rental customer. Those stages should not share a denominator just because each number has MW after it.

This is not an answer to every bear concern. Poor utilisation, lower prices and costly delays can all be real. Matching the population and period lets us identify them rather than manufacture them through the calculation.

For $SPCX, show the capacity that actually billed during the period, at the prices it actually earned, and separate it from what was still being installed. Then we can have a much better argument about demand.

The ten-megawatt example is illustrative, not a claim about a disclosed customer contract.

The most dangerous feature of $CIFR downside is the feedback loop between financing terms, equity issuance, and the stock price itself.

Weaker project financing increases the parent equity requirement, which forces more issuance, while a lower share price means each financing round requires even more shares to raise the necessary capital.

Our model captures that dynamic through average net issue prices of $12 in bear, $22 in base, and $35 in bull, with bear requiring $5.37 billion of external equity and 447 million shares versus $292 million and roughly 8 million shares in bull.

That creates an 18 times difference in external capital requirements despite only a 26% difference in physical platform size, turning financing conditions into a much larger driver of per share outcomes than operating capacity.

The mechanism also works in reverse, as stronger financing reduces equity needs, supports the share price, lowers dilution per dollar raised, and creates a compounding advantage for subsequent funding rounds.

MediaTek’s latest announcement on the deepening of its long-term partnership with Nvidia repeatedly uses the term “rack-scale.” This is the key to understanding the announcement, and it directly validates the central conclusion of my research from more than two months ago:

MediaTek has upgraded the strategic positioning of its AI business from "IC / ASIC design" to "system-level design."

The announcement link:
https://t.co/Yf4XOFVvSH

The announcement also explains how MediaTek plans to put this new positioning into practice. By working with Nvidia, MediaTek can bring custom chips and XPUs into Nvidia’s mature rack-scale ecosystem, so that once chip development is complete, they can be integrated more quickly into rack-scale systems for deployment in data centers and AI factories.

For MediaTek, Nvidia’s mature rack-scale systems ecosystem means it does not need to start from scratch, giving this new strategy a much clearer path to execution.

For Nvidia, MediaTek’s custom silicon design capabilities and customer base can help extend Nvidia’s rack-scale ecosystem further into the custom silicon market.

This also explains why “rack-scale” is the key term in the announcement: it is where the two companies need each other most. MediaTek can move from chips to systems, while Nvidia can extend its rack-scale ecosystem into the custom silicon market, creating a win-win that opens up new growth opportunities for both.

author.name: 郭明錤｜Ming-Chi Kuo
author.description: 香港天風國際證券分析師，分享科技產業趨勢觀察｜TF International Securities (HK) analyst sharing tech trend insights

mingchikuo.text:
Just as the market had come to believe that Rubin CPX had been dropped from Nvidia’s product roadmap, my latest industry checks indicate that Nvidia has revived the program, with production expected to begin in 1Q27. Compared with the previous design, the revived Rubin CPX delivers stronger prefill performance and features major changes to both its GPU specifications and rack architecture, underscoring the high priority Nvidia places on prefill solutions.

Key changes:

1. Rubin CPX GPU specs
CPX delivers near-Rubin compute performance and matches Rubin’s maximum power rating of 2,300 W per GPU. CPX moves to 168 GB of HBM4, vs. 288 GB on Rubin and 128 GB of GDDR7 on the previous CPX design.

2. Rack design
The new CPX uses a standalone MGX ETL rack rather than sharing a rack with Rubin, as in the previous design. Customers can opt for 64, 128, 192, or 256 CPX GPUs depending on their needs. Within a CPX rack, each group of 64 CPX GPUs forms a rack module comprising eight compute trays (eight CPX GPUs per tray) and one switch tray.

3. Scale-up and scale-out
NVLink is used only for scale-up among the eight CPX GPUs within each tray, with 1–1.5 TB/s of NVLink bandwidth per CPX (vs. 3.6 TB/s per Rubin). Inter-tray scale-out within each rack module runs over Spectrum-6 Ethernet using all-copper L1 links. Across rack modules, scale-out is handled by each module’s Spectrum-6 switch over OSFP optical links.

4. How it works
CPX must be paired with Vera Rubin NVL72, and Nvidia recommends a 1:1 ratio of CPX to Rubin GPUs. CPX handles prefill and builds the KV cache, which is then transferred to Rubin over Ethernet RDMA for decode.

5. Product positioning: Best performance per dollar for long-context prefill
Over 50% of today’s AI inference workload comes from processing input context and building the corresponding KV cache. CPX therefore offers a more flexible, lower-cost way to handle prefill. Each eight-CPX tray has approximately 1.34 TB of HBM4, sufficient for most long-context prefill workloads and associated KV cache requirements.

author.description: 香港天風國際證券分析師，分享科技產業趨勢觀察｜TF International Securities (HK) analyst sharing tech trend insights

mingchikuo.text:
正當市場認為 Rubin CPX 已被 Nvidia 從產品藍圖中移除之際，我最新的產業調查顯示，Nvidia 已重啟 Rubin CPX，預計於 1Q27 開始生產。相較舊版，重啟後的 Rubin CPX 擁有更強的預填充（prefill）效能，GPU 規格與機櫃架構也都有明顯改變，足以證明 Nvidia 對 prefill 方案的高度重視。

關鍵改變如下：

1. Rubin CPX GPU 規格
CPX 算力接近 Rubin，單顆 GPU 最高功耗也同為 2,300 W。CPX 記憶體改為 168 GB HBM4，低於 Rubin 的 288 GB HBM4，但高於舊版 CPX 的 128 GB GDDR7。

2. 機櫃設計
新版 CPX 採用獨立的 MGX ETL 機櫃，不再像舊版與 Rubin 共櫃。客戶可依需求配置 64、128、192 或 256 顆 CPX。在 CPX 機櫃中，每 64 顆 CPX 組成一個機櫃模組，每個機櫃模組配置 8 個運算托盤（每個托盤有 8 顆 CPX）與 1 個交換機托盤。

3. Scale-up 與 scale-out
NVLink 僅用於同一托盤內 8 顆 CPX GPU 的 scale-up，每顆 CPX 的 NVLink 頻寬為 1–1.5 TB/s（vs. 每顆 Rubin 的 3.6 TB/s）。同一機櫃模組內的托盤間，透過 Spectrum-6 Ethernet（全銅 L1）進行 scale-out；跨機櫃模組時，則由各模組的 Spectrum-6 透過 OSFP 光纖進行 scale-out。

4. 運作方式
CPX 需與 Vera Rubin NVL72 搭配，Nvidia 建議 CPX 與 Rubin 的比例為 1:1。CPX 負責預填充（prefill）並建立 KV cache，再透過 Ethernet RDMA 傳給 Rubin 執行解碼生成（decode）。

5. 產品定位：長上下文 prefill 的最高性價比方案
目前 AI 推論工作量中，超過一半來自處理輸入內容（context）並建立相對應的 KV cache，因此，CPX 以更彈性的部署方式與更低成本承接 prefill。每個運算托盤（有 8 個 CPX）約有 1.34 TB HBM4，足以支援大多數長上下文 prefill 與 KV cache 建立需求。
